'''Aaron Shawn Holiday''' (born September 30, 1996) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]]. The [[guard (basketball)|guard]] played in high school in Los Angeles, where he was ranked among the top players nationally. Holiday was a [[starting lineup|starter]] as a college freshman in 2015–16 before becoming the Bruins' leading [[Substitution (sport)|reserve]] the following year. As a junior, he returned to the starting lineup as the Bruins' [[point guard]], and earned [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] recognition as well as first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|all-conference]] and all-defensive honors in the [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball|Pac-12]]. He is the younger brother of [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) players [[Jrue Holiday|Jrue]] and [[Justin Holiday]].

==College career==
===Freshman season===
Holiday entered [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]] with a reputation as a tenacious defender capable of applying full-court pressure.<ref>{{cite news|last=Rothstein |first=John |title=Observations: UCLA freshman guard Aaron Holiday will have a major role |date=October 29, 2015 |website=CBSSports.com |url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/25357386/observations-ucla-freshman-guard-aaron-holiday-will-have-a-major-role |archiveurl=https://www.webcitation.org/6dfI68GQq?url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/25357386/observations-ucla-freshman-guard-aaron-holiday-will-have-a-major-role |archivedate=December 10, 2015 |deadurl=no |df= }}</ref> After an exhibition game against the Bruins, [[Cal State Los Angeles Golden Eagles men's basketball|Cal State Los Angeles]] coach Dieter Horton admired his ability to disrupt, calling him a "little [[Tasmanian devil]] on defense".<ref>{{cite news|last=Eisenberg |first=Jeff |title=West Coast Bias: Opposing coaches assess five of this year's top teams |date=November 4, 2015 |work=The Dagger |publisher=Yahoo! Sports! |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/ncaab-the-dagger/west-coast-bias--opposing-coaches-assess-five-of-this-year-s-top-teams-172713525.html |archiveurl=https://www.webcitation.org/6dff2E4ny?url=http://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/ncaab-the-dagger/west-coast-bias--opposing-coaches-assess-five-of-this-year-s-top-teams-172713525.html |archivedate=December 10, 2015 |deadurl=no |df= }}</ref> Holiday and fellow recruit Prince Ali brought needed depth to UCLA, who were thin at guard during the [[2014–15 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|previous season]]. In Holiday, Bruins' third-year coach [[Steve Alford]] possessed the most natural [[point guard]] he had had at the school. He hoped the freshman could help ease ball-handling duties from incumbent point guard [[Bryce Alford]], the coach's son, who was more effective catching the ball and shooting.<ref>{{cite news|last=Helfand |first=Zach |title=Freshmen Prince Ali, Aaron Holiday bring needed jolt to UCLA backcourt |date=September 1, 2015 |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-basketball-20150901-story.html |archiveurl=https://www.webcitation.org/6dfTzM88f?url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-basketball-20150901-story.html |archivedate=December 10, 2015 |deadurl=no |df= }}</ref>  In a scrimmage against [[San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball|San Diego State]] which Bryce Alford mostly missed due to an injury, Holiday's performance against a strong Aztecs defense prompted their coach, [[Steve Fisher]], to call him "by far the best player on the floor".<ref name=helfand_11132015>{{cite news|last=Helfand |first=Zach |title=Freshman Aaron Holiday brings energy and swarming defense to UCLA |date=November 13, 2015 |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-basketball-holiday-20151113-story.html |archiveurl=https://www.webcitation.org/6dcZhtwdR?url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-basketball-holiday-20151113-story.html |archivedate=December 8, 2015 |deadurl=no |df= }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Holiday is the youngest of four children. Brothers [[Jrue Holiday|Jrue]] and [[Justin Holiday|Justin]] are currently professional basketball players who play in the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]]. Jrue also attended UCLA, as did sister Lauren, who played on the [[UCLA Bruins women's basketball|Bruins women's basketball team]]. Additionally, he is a brother-in-law of [[United States women's national soccer team|USA women's soccer international]] [[Lauren Holiday]].<ref name=ucla_bio/>
